scope: Side-effect-free diagnostic stack inspection, not a production graphics behavior change.
problem: An extended 256-word MMIO capture crossed an unmapped native stack page. CPU.translate_address_system_read calls the normal faulting translator and unwraps its result; catching its JS exception did not undo the guest #PF. The native-dispatch trial logged a Rust panic and subsequently reset the driver. That trial is invalid as graphics evidence.
change: MMIO, RAMIN and RAMHT diagnostic stacks now walk current x86 page tables directly in ordinary RAM. Missing/out-of-RAM addresses remain null. No guest exception, TLB fill, A/D bit update or MMIO is performed. Captures remain bounded at 256 words; default MMIO capture stays 16.
validation: Paging-disabled, 4 KiB, cross-page unaligned DWORD, PSE 4 MiB, PAE 4 KiB/NX and 2 MiB mappings.
Missing pages, high physical pages, 32-bit wrap and a 256-word capture at a stack boundary preserve CR2 and guest RAM exactly.
node --check on the shared guest harness.

nativeProof.guest: XP 93.71, original cold 2001 SE run restored at its coherent pre-fault checkpoint.
nativeProof.result: Original ISR read trap, context, class=0x4097, instance=0xE9B6, source/status and resumed via 0x400720=1. Extended capture has no Rust panic or instrumentation-triggered reset. Native suite remains under investigation.

limits: The earlier 16-word/native runs without absent-page faults remain separate evidence; the invalid extended trial is not used to claim a hardware defect or fix.
Raw stack values are module candidates, not an unwound call stack.
